requirements.statement: The page keeps the real service's mechanics: its address under the notification (commodities/identification), its entry guard, a CSRF crumb and concurrency token on every post, server-side validation only, values that fail validation never saved, and errors shown only on the response to the failing submission.
requirements.why: Persistence, authentication and validation are real constraints the prototype cannot express, and the ruling lets them override it.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-074, repo-frontend-p10-175 and trace-animals-fit-p10-014 show the column headed 'Number of animals' today.

requirements.statement: Each identifier belongs to one animal: the page holds a set of identifier values per animal, not one set for the commodity line or for the notification.
requirements.why: V4 applies every animal identifier at unit level, so the trader is asked to identify each animal in turn rather than the line as a whole.

requirements.statement: Every identifier value comes from the trader: the fields start empty and none is filled in from another system.
requirements.why: V4 names the user as the source of every animal identifier, so no identifier is looked up or prefilled.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-136 shows the ear tag and passport empty when the page opens.

requirements.statement: A species panel shows only the identifier fields its commodity requires; a field for an identifier the commodity does not require is absent from the page, not hidden.
requirements.why: V4 makes each identifier conditional on the selected commodity requiring it, which is also how the real service and DR2.1 build the panel.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-090 builds a card's fields from the commodity code's declared identifiers filtered by what applies to the species, and repo-frontend-p10-096 and repo-frontend-p10-097 show a pet line and a pig line asked for those fields and nothing else.

requirements.statement: A species may be asked for more than one kind of identifier at once, and no rule limits how many of them one animal's record holds.
requirements.why: V4's identifier commodity lists overlap, so one commodity can require a passport, a tattoo and an ear tag together, and the page sets no upper bound on how many a trader fills in.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-093 shows a cattle line asked for three identifiers at once, repo-frontend-p10-109 a column for each of them, repo-frontend-p10-179 one saved animal holding several identifiers and reading each back, and repo-frontend-p10-144 that an animal may be saved on one of them alone with no upper bound on how many are filled in.

requirements.statement: Which identifier fields a species panel shows follows the species, not the commodity code alone, so two species sharing a code can be asked for different identifiers: on 0101 a horse panel asks for a horse name while a donkey, pony, zebra or mule panel does not.
requirements.why: The policy page's identifier commodity lists name a species beside each code, and code 0101 appears five times in the passport list but once in the horse name list, so a panel built on the code alone would ask the wrong questions.

requirements.statement: A 'Passport' identifier is asked for on every species whose commodity V4 names: 0101 donkeys and asses, horses, ponies, zebras, and mules, hinnies or other hybrids; 0102 cattle; and 01061900 cats, dogs and ferrets.
requirements.why: V4 is the specification of which commodities each identifier rule covers, and its passport list agrees with DR2.1 on every commodity today's catalogue holds.

requirements.statement: An identifier value is free text: within its length limit any value is accepted, and no identifier has a format rule.
requirements.why: V4 types every animal identifier as a string with a maximum length and gives its example values as examples only, setting no pattern; the real service checks nothing but the length.

requirements.statement: A species whose commodity requires none of passport, tattoo, ear tag or horse name is asked for 'Identification details', a 20-character-wide text input with a label and no hint, holding free text that identifies the animals.
requirements.why: V4 gives every commodity without a specific identifier type a free-text identifier, so a trader importing salmon, bees or poultry can still say what identifies the animals; V4 is the specification of which data a notification captures and outranks DR2.1, which asks nothing of such a species.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-091 and repo-frontend-p10-092 show the field offered for any commodity and labelled 'Identification details', repo-frontend-p10-099 its twenty-character width and absent hint, and repo-tests-p1-153 an ostrich line answering it end to end.

requirements.statement: The same species is asked for 'Description', a 20-character-wide text input with a label and no hint, holding a free-text description of the animals.
requirements.why: V4 pairs a description with the free-text identification details for a commodity with no specific identifier type, so the pair together identifies the animals.

conflicts.about: Whether the page takes the prototype's mount mechanics (its own URL, no entry guards, its own field names and button values, invalid values saved).

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, validation and authentication, overrides the prototype.
The prototype never decides URL paths or form field names.

A Remove button posts remove:<species>:<index>.
A refused page is served with a bad-request status and nothing invalid is saved.
The page accepts the service's own field names, indexed by commodity line.

conflicts.outcome: Both rulings rank first. The 7 October ruling names persistence, validation and authentication as constraints that override the prototype, and the 9 October ruling adds that the prototype never decides URL paths or form field names. The page keeps the real address under its notification, its guard, CSRF and concurrency token, its own field names, ids and button values (repo-tests-p1-152), and never saves invalid values (repo-frontend-p10-134).

conflicts.about: Whether the real identifier length limit and stale-action safeguards stay where Design Release 2.1 has none.

positions.says: Validation the prototype cannot express overrides it.
No live-animal text field has a length limit, so a live-animal value is never rejected for its content.
A panel save for a species with no animal left to enter does nothing.
A remove for a position that does not exist is ignored; removing the last saved animal deletes the species' record.
No identifier may be longer than 58 characters.
A further record on a full line is refused with the cap-reached message.
A removal naming a record position the line does not hold is refused as a bad request.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first, and V4 gives every identifier a 58-character limit: the limit (repo-frontend-p10-125), the cap-reached error for a stale add (repo-frontend-p10-130) and the bad request for a bad remove (repo-frontend-p10-116) stay. Where the prototype words the same kind of rule, its wording is used: '<label> must be 58 characters or less'. prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-066 is not overruled: its other half, that removing the last animal deletes the species' record, still stands.

conflicts.about: When an animal (or a germinal entry) counts as identified, and what bar the Complete status sets: one identifier filled, or every identifier its species asks for and every animal entered.

positions.says: One identifier is enough for an animal to count as entered.
The Complete status uses the submit bar.
DR1 inc-103 is closed and not built.
The prototype wins by default over today's service.

inc-103 is deferred for adjudication.
Whether DR1's every-identifier bar or V4's at-least-one governs is open.
The frontend counts an animal as identified once one identifier is filled, matching V4.
DR1 lists only complete animals and keeps the trader on a partly filled one.
The identifier block is satisfied by at least one of its fields, each optional on its own.
A record is saved only when at least one identifier field holds something.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first and answers this difference directly. One identifier is enough: a live animal saved with at least one identifier is entered, listed in the saved table and moved past; the Complete status uses exactly the submit bar, with no stricter bar of its own; DR1 inc-103 is closed and not built. Design Release 2.1 now agrees for live animals (prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-058, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-032), so only its germinal readings are set aside: a germinal entry counts once it holds at least one value, neither because it was merely saved (prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-069) nor only once every field is filled (the germinal half of prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-116, whose live half stands). The policy page agrees: every one of its six animal identifier fields is optional on its own while the block is satisfied by at least one (confluence-6497338582-p4-005). This is what the service does today (repo-frontend-p10-120). repo-frontend-p10-120 and document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-016 back the winning rule and are not overruled; ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-008 still stands as the general look-and-feel default. How many animals and species must hold such a record before submit is not settled here: that question is c-336, and the germinal twin is c-277.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first: one identifier is enough, so a partly filled animal saves with no error and the panel moves on. DR1's per-identifier errors were asked for only if every identifier were ruled required, which the ruling closes (c-041), so they are not built. An animal with no identifier at all is refused, which Design Release 2.1 now does too, so its wording wins over today's: 'Enter at least one identifier' on a panel with more than one identifier, and the field named, such as 'Enter an ear tag', on a panel with one (req-234, req-animal-identification-006). Save and continue and Save and return never block on missing identifiers, as in the prototype. repo-frontend-p10-121 is not overruled: it is the evidence of today's wording that the change requirements cite.
